record.paper_title: The Lieb-Thirring inequalities: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Characterize all potentials V in L^1(R^2) — or at least all nonpositive V in L^1(R^2) — for which the two-dimensional Schrödinger operator has asymptotically linear eigenvalue counting under coupling, that is, either lim sup_{α→∞} α^(-1) N(−Δ + αV) < ∞ or the two-dimensional Weyl-type asymptotic formula holds.

evidence.quote: In particular, the paper [110] raises the question of characterizing all V ∈ L1(R2) (or all 0 ≥ V ∈ L1(R2)) such that either lim supα→∞ α−1N(−∆ + αV ) < ∞ or such that (24) with d = 2 and γ = 0 holds.
This problem was solved in the radial case in [110], but is still open in general.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V \in L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ be a real-valued potential, and for $\alpha > 0$ consider the Schrödinger operator $-\Delta + \alpha V$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ defined via the standard quadratic form. Let $N(-\Delta + \alpha V)$ denote the number of negative eigenvalues of this operator (counted with multiplicities). The semiclassical Weyl-type formula in dimension $d=2$ at coupling $\alpha$ reads
$$\lim_{\alpha\to\infty}\alpha^{-1}\,N(-\Delta+\alpha V)=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb{R}^2}V_-(x)\,dx,\qquad V_-:=\max(-V,0).$$
Provide a complete characterization of all $V\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ — and, separately, of all nonpositive $V\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ (i.e. $V\le 0$ a.e.) — such that either
$$\limsup_{\alpha\to\infty}\alpha^{-1}\,N(-\Delta+\alpha V)<\infty,$$
or the Weyl asymptotic formula displayed above holds. (For radially symmetric potentials such a characterization is known; the problem asks for a characterization without symmetry assumptions.)
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of characterizing 2D potentials yielding linear-in-coupling growth of the negative eigenvalue count, or Weyl asymptotics, has been resolved only in the radial case (Laptev–Solomyak and related work). Recent surveys on Lieb–Thirring inequalities and the paper "Negative Eigenvalues of Two-Dimensional Schrödinger Operators" indicate the general (non-radial) problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: The state of the Lieb–Thirring conjecture (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses 2D anomalous behavior and the open problem of characterizing potentials with linear eigenvalue growth/Weyl asymptotics; resolved only in radial case.
status_evidence.claim: The general (non-radial) characterization remains open, while the radial case is solved.

status_evidence.title: Negative Eigenvalues of Two-Dimensional Schrödinger Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the 2D negative eigenvalue counting function and obtains sharp bounds, motivating the characterization question for general potentials.
status_evidence.claim: The 2D N(-Δ+αV) behavior is subtle and the full characterization is not available beyond the radial setting.
